description: Our goal is to create an educational game about space station docking missions.
summary:
Vector Align is a browser-based 3D spacecraft simulator spanning four missions (Liftoff, Station Docking, Station Departure, Capsule Landing) across 16 progressive levels with telemetry and debriefs.
Powered by a deterministic physics engine and Three.js, it pairs aerospace models (1976 U.S. Standard Atmosphere, Mach-dependent drag, Max-Q, staging, Saturn V data) with NASA open 3D assets (SLS/Artemis, Saturn V, ISS, Blue Marble). Modeled wind gusts let learners compare Manual piloting against Hold Pitch SAS.
By turning concepts like 6-DOF inertia and reentry blackout into free, zero-account browser training in seven languages across desktop and mobile, Vector Align makes spaceflight education globally accessible.
details:
### What It Does & How It Works

**Vector Align · Orbital Academy** is an offline-capable 3D browser game for the **Space Mission Design Game** challenge. Across **4 mission phases and 16 progressive levels**, players manually pilot an end-to-end NASA-inspired flight arc:

1. **Liftoff** (Saturn V & SLS Block 1): Gravity turn, Max-Q, staging, and ~7.8 km/s LEO insertion.

2. **Station Docking**: 6-DOF approach to the **ISS Harmony port**, mastering inertia and soft capture (unlocks Free Flight).

3. **Station Departure**: Spring push-off, 0–5 m thruster plume keep-out coast, and corridor alignment.

4. **Capsule Landing**: 80–38 km plasma blackout attitude hold, dual parachutes, and ~1.5 m retro-rockets.

A deterministic **60 Hz physics engine** (modeling the US Standard Atmosphere 1976 and live Keplerian orbit elements) runs decoupled from 3D rendering. Levels 1–3 isolate single skills before Level 4 combines them, with 5 Hz post-flight debrief curves and local IndexedDB progress—zero accounts or backend needed.

### Benefits & Impact

Turns counterintuitive orbital physics into hands-on gameplay on any desktop or mobile browser, offline after first load and available in **7 languages** for zero-barrier STEM education.

### Tools, Tech & NASA Data

Built on a standard laptop with **TypeScript, React 19, Three.js (`@react-three/fiber`), Zustand, Vite, Workbox PWA, Blender, Vitest (133 passing tests), and Playwright**, grounded in NASA's open ISS 3D model, Blue Marble texture, and Saturn V AS-506 / Artemis I public data (independent educational project).

### Innovation & Solo Considerations

As a **solo developer**, I used a 4-layer architecture (`Pure Sim → Headless Test Driver → UI → Render-Only 3D`) with shared camera controls so all 16 levels could be built and verified rapidly without WebGL, compressed the ISS model (~44.5 MB → ~12.8 MB) for mobile performance, and openly documented all teaching simplifications in-app.
